audio.strategy: Sampled multi-piano instrument with a live-DSP effect chain, plus generated Organ and Synth engines sharing the same audio graph. Primary piano sound: eight bundled RECORDED sample sets across the six selectable piano types — Grand/Upright/Electric/Digital bundle one model each, Clav and Misc each bundle a SECOND model (Clavinet+Harpsichord, Vibraphone+Marimba — spec.scope.optional model list view) — played through AudioBufferSourceNodes with nearest-root selection, recorded-velocity-layer crossfading (grand) or declared gain+filter velocity shaping (single-layer sets), unison detune copies, and per-voice envelopes. Organ and Synth are GENERATED live Web Audio additive/subtractive/oscillator synthesis, never recordings, declared as digital models throughout. One shared AudioContext: Piano voices enter per-layer buses (timbre EQ, dynamic compression, level); Organ layers feed one shared effect chain; each Synth layer (A/B/C) has its own independent effect chain. Every chain is the same ordered unit list Mod 1 → Mod 2 → Delay → Amp Sim/EQ → Compressor → Reverb, then either the single Rotary Speaker instance (Amp unit 'To Rotary', or the Organ strip's dedicated ORGAN rotary-source button) or directly the master gain → limiter → one destination. All effects are live Web Audio processing (LFOs, modulated delays, biquads, waveshapers, convolution). The Phase 1 oscillator voice survives only as a clearly labeled synthesized fallback after primary piano sample failure.

generatedSources.name: Synthesized fallback voice
generatedSources.notes: Used ONLY after primary sample failure (or a minimal reduced graph) and labeled 'FALLBACK … synthesized' in the status strip and Program display. Never presented as recorded material.

generatedSources.name: Reverb impulse responses
generatedSources.kind: algorithmically generated buffers (deterministic xorshift noise, per-type decay/predelay/spring character)
generatedSources.notes: Six reverb types use generated IRs through a ConvolverNode — generated DSP, not recorded spaces.

generatedSources.name: String-resonance impulse and pedal-noise thump
generatedSources.notes: String Res is a generated sympathetic-resonance approximation active with the damper lifted (the spec's pedal-down samples are not available); Ped Noise is a generated filtered thump. Both are declared approximations, never recordings.

generatedSources.name: Organ section engines (B3, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1, B3 Bass, Pipe 2)
generatedSources.notes: Digital MODELS, never recordings: B3 = nine sine tonewheel partials with generated key click, single-triggered (or POLY, via Shift + Percussion Volume) percussion and a modulated-delay vib/chorus scanner; Vox = sawtooth partials with a filtered/unfiltered tone-mix drawbar; Farf = square/saw register switches; Pipe 1 = detuned sine ranks with a generated chiff. Two spec-optional models extend the cycle: B3 Bass reuses B3's tonewheel partials and key click but only wires the 16'+8' drawbars (every other drawbar is silent, no percussion); Pipe 2 reuses Pipe 1's ranks/chiff with a brighter principal registration (triangle waveform on the bottom three ranks, boosted level and wider ensemble detune on the top five). Drawbars retarget sounding voices live. Both Organ layers share one effect chain (manual p. 18). Simplifications (no tonewheel folding/wear, approximated register filters) are declared in src/audio/organ-models.ts.

generatedSources.name: Effect processing (Mod 1/Mod 2/Delay/Amp-EQ/Compressor/Rotary)
generatedSources.kind: live Web Audio DSP (LFO-modulated gains/panners/filters/delays, feedback delay loop with in-loop filtering, waveshaper drive, DynamicsCompressor, dual-band rotary with inertial speed ramps)
generatedSources.notes: Every unit processes real audio through connected nodes with click-free crossfaded bypass; no unit is a label, enum or disconnected node. Piano layers A/B, the shared Organ chain, and each Synth layer A/B/C all get their own independent instance of this same ordered chain; the single Rotary Speaker instance is shared by whichever chains route 'To Rotary' or use the Organ strip's ORGAN source button.

generatedSources.name: Synth oscillator sources (Analog mode: Pure/Sync/Multi/Super/FM-H)
generatedSources.notes: Every required waveform is GENERATED, never recorded. Pure uses native oscillator types (Sine/Triangle/Saw/Square) plus PeriodicWaves built from an asymmetric-duty square's Fourier series for Pulse 33/10, and a looping generated xorshift buffer for White Noise. Sync Saw/Square are a DECLARED spectral approximation of hard sync — not a real two-oscillator reset mechanism, but a PeriodicWave whose harmonic energy is shaped by a gaussian resonance bump that Osc Ctrl sweeps, reproducing the audible signature (a moving formant) honestly labeled as an approximation. Multi Saw/8ve are 3-4 real detuned sawtooth oscillators. Super Saw/Square are a real 7-oscillator unison stack, alternately panned. FM 2-op is genuine two-operator FM synthesis: a 1:1-ratio modulator's output gain feeds the carrier oscillator's frequency AudioParam directly.

generatedSources.name: Synth filter, envelopes (amp/filter/osc) and LFO
generatedSources.notes: Per-voice filter: a real WaveShaperNode drive stage (Off/1/2/3, the same tanh-saturation curve shape as the Rotary Speaker's drive) feeds one BiquadFilterNode (LP12/HP/BP) or two cascaded lowpass stages in series (LP24 — a genuine 24 dB/octave slope, never a label or a steeper Q on one stage). Keyboard tracking scales the base cutoff by note position. All three envelopes (amp/filter/osc) schedule real AudioParam ramps: the filter envelope sweeps the tracked base cutoff toward an envAmount-scaled peak and back; the oscillator envelope targets either real pitch (every source oscillator's detune) or the same live Osc Ctrl target Osc Ctrl itself retargets (FM-H's true modulation-index gain, or a declared approximation gain summed into detune for Sync/Multi/Super). One standing LFO per synth layer (five real generated waveforms — native oscillator types, an inverted-gain Saw Down, and a generated xorshift Sample & Hold buffer) connects its depth gain directly to the chosen destination's real AudioParam(s): oscillator detune, filter frequency, or the live Osc Ctrl target.

generatedSources.name: Synth voice modes (Mono/Legato/priority/glide/unison/vibrato) and arpeggiator/gate
generatedSources.kind: live Web Audio oscillator retargeting + a deterministic JS scheduler
generatedSources.notes: Mono always retriggers a fresh envelope on a new note, releasing the previous one. Legato reuses the sounding voice and glides every source oscillator's frequency to the new note via setTargetAtTime (a real constant-rate portamento) — no envelope retrigger, no new nodes. Priority Low/High makes the lower/higher of two held notes win the sounding voice while the loser waits on a held-note stack; releasing the winner returns to the next-priority held note. Unison duplicates the layer's fundamental waveform 2/4/6 times with detune/pan/gain (reusing the piano section's own unison math). Vibrato is a per-layer sine LFO whose frequency follows the panel-editable Rate (spec voice.vibrato.menu: 2.0-8.0 Hz linear, default ~5.5 Hz) and whose depth scales with the panel-editable Amount (displayed 0-10) in On/Delayed mode, or the live mod-wheel/control-pedal position scaled by that same Amount in Wheel/Pedal mode. The VIBRATO MENU button latches the Synth OLED's dials 1/2 onto Rate/Amount editing, mutually exclusive with the AMP/FILTER/OSC envelope dial-repurposing. The arpeggiator/gate is a section-level scheduler on the injected timer boundary (a self-rescheduling setTimeout chain, cleared on ARP RUN off or dispose): Arp mode steps the held-note set (expanded 1-4 octaves) in Up/Down/Up-Down/Random order through the ordinary startSynthVoice path; Gate mode starts no new voices at all and instead pulses already-sounding voices' gain between full and a hardness floor. KB HOLD keeps the held-note set (and the arp's cycle through it) alive after physical key-up. The ARP MENU button (manual p. 35) latches the Synth OLED dials onto page / setting / setting across all five menu pages: 1 Direction/Zig Zag, 2 Pattern Preset/Length, 3 Pattern Edit (per-step gate Off/On/Long), 4 Pattern Accent, 5 Pattern Pan (L/C/R). PATTERN (Shift + Arp Mode) makes the arp/gate conform to the 2-16 step pattern: silent steps cut real holes in the rhythm without skipping arpeggio notes (a separate melodic counter advances only on sounding steps), accents raise step velocity (audible when a velocity-sensitive parameter is active, per the manual's own note), Long steps ring into the next step while normal steps close their per-voice gate stage early, and panned steps route the voice through a StereoPanner before the layer bus; the preset table is an honest stand-in (Nord's exact factory patterns are unpublished). GROUP (Shift + Arp Menu) is a declared adaptation of the manual's all-Layers sharing: this build's single section-level arp drives every enabled layer with Group On and only the focused layer with Group Off (the full per-layer arpeggiator stays out of scope). Zig Zag reorders the directed sequences two-steps-forward-one-back via a pure step-counter walk; pattern/group/zigZag are snapshot-stored on synth.arp with backfill, and Random's deterministic xorshift draw is untouched.

generatedSources.name: LP M and LP+HP filter types (optional scope)
generatedSources.kind: live Web Audio biquad cascade + waveshaper approximation
generatedSources.notes: LP M is a DECLARED approximation of the hardware's self-oscillating ladder-style lowpass: the same two-lowpass-stage cascade as LP24, but the second stage's Q is mapped 1.5x hotter than the first (and than LP24's identical-Q pair), plus an always-on fixed drive waveshaper stage ahead of the cascade (distinct from, and in addition to, the user-facing Drive-knob shaper) — not a true nonlinear ladder-filter feedback topology. LP+HP pairs one lowpass stage at the tracked cutoff with one highpass stage fixed 2 octaves below it, giving a wider/shallower passband than BP's single resonant stage; this is a real two-stage series filter, not an approximation of the pairing itself. Both types share LP24/LP12/HP/BP's keyboard tracking, resonance, drive and filter-envelope wiring unchanged.

generatedSources.name: Sub Osc, Shape, Shape Sine, Wave and FM-I oscillator categories (optional scope)
generatedSources.notes: Saw Sub / Square Sub: a real main oscillator plus a real square sub-oscillator one octave down; Osc Ctrl is that sub's gain (0..1), a true linear AudioParam, live-retargetable on a sounding voice — no spectral approximation. Shape Pulse (its own category, distinct from Shape Sine per spec.scope.optional's 'Shape, Shape Sine' listing): a PeriodicWave pulse whose duty cycle follows Osc Ctrl, rebuilt on quantized ctrl steps like Sync's moving spectral peak — a real duty-cycle Fourier series, stepped rather than continuously morphed. Shape Sine (separate category): a sine oscillator through a wavefolding WaveShaper curve; Osc Ctrl is a live pre-shaper drive gain (fold amount, a true linear AudioParam), while the fold curve itself is generated once per quantized ctrl step — declared generated DSP. Wave Organ / Wave Formant: two fixed digital PeriodicWaves (an organ drawbar-partial recipe and a vowel-formant-like bump spectrum) built once; Osc Ctrl has no effect for this category, spec-consistent with Pure's 'No effect' rule. FM 2-op B (FM-I): identical two-operator FM structure to FM-H's FM 2-op, but a 1.414 (inharmonic) modulator:carrier ratio instead of 1:1 — true FM synthesis, Osc Ctrl is still the real modulation-index gain.

generatedSources.name: Synth Samples mode (optional scope)
generatedSources.kind: recorded AudioBufferSourceNode voices (nearest-root + playbackRate pitch shift)
generatedSources.notes: Samples mode swaps the per-voice source construction from the Analog oscillator switch to AudioBufferSourceNode voices built from the bundled SYNTH_SAMPLE_SETS (Strings/Choir — see sampleSources above), picking the nearest recorded root via nearestSynthZone and pitch-shifting with playbackRate; unison duplicates re-play the same nearest-root buffer as detuned/panned copies (mirroring the piano section's own unison pattern), and each set's declared per-set gain is applied like the piano library's spec.gain. The shared amp/filter/filter-envelope stage (built once per voice, downstream of source construction) applies unchanged to Samples-mode voices, so FREQ/RES/keyboard tracking audibly darken or brighten a sample voice exactly as they do an oscillator voice. DECLARED LIMITATION: the oscillator envelope's toPitch mode and vibrato/LFO 'Osc Pitch' destination retarget a sample voice's playbackRate through a small per-source cents-to-rate-ratio translator gain (the SAME cents-shaped depth gains the Analog path uses, summed onto playbackRate instead of dropped) rather than a literal pitch-cents AudioParam — an honest best-effort connection, not a claim of the exact same mechanism as Analog detune modulation. Osc Ctrl and the non-toPitch oscillator-envelope/LFO 'Osc Ctrl' destination have no effect in Samples mode (there is no per-category Osc Ctrl target for a recorded voice), shown on the OLED as OSC CTRL: —.

notes: All recorded material was obtained exclusively through the npm registry (the run's only permitted network source) and is bundled under public/samples/ for fully offline playback; see public/samples/SOURCES.md and scripts/sync-samples.mjs for the exact provenance chain.

One AudioContext feeds per-layer buses, ordered effects (Piano layers, the shared Organ chain, and each Synth layer's own independent chain), the single rotary instance, master gain and limiter into one destination; no engine or effect creates a parallel context or destination.

All six piano types (Grand/Upright/Electric/Clav/Digital/Misc) bundle a recorded model, and Clav and Misc each bundle a SECOND recorded model (Harpsichord, Marimba — spec.scope.optional 'More than one model per type and the model list view'); the missing-model state (spec: nord-stage-4.piano.json selection.missingModelState — flashing type LED, truthful Program-display report, labeled playable fallback) is reached through sample load failure. While Shift is latched, turning the Piano Model dial shows the focused layer's type's model list on the Program OLED, mirroring the Shift + Program dial numeric list view.

SOLO (manual p. 18): holding a Piano/Organ/Synth section's ON button for roughly half a second, or Shift + clicking the same button (a keyboard-accessible equivalent, since long-press isn't reachable without a pointer), activates only that section and turns the other two off. sectionOn fields are ordinary snapshot state, so a solo round-trips through Store/recall like any other program edit.

The brand wordmark ('nord stage 4') renders with Comfortaa (SIL Open Font License 1.1, The Comfortaa Project Authors), bundled via the @fontsource/comfortaa npm package so the woff2 is inlined into the production build and the logotype renders identically fully offline, with no system-font or network-font dependency.

Sustain pedal input arrives three ways per the spec: the on-screen latching SUSTAIN PEDAL control in the status strip, the Space key, and MIDI CC64 (continuous half-pedal). SUSTPED (Shift + Layer A) and PSTICK (Shift + Layer B) route the sustain pedal and pitch stick to their section per the manual (p. 18/23), with panel LEDs showing the routing state, for Piano, Organ and each Synth layer.

Functional controls: keybed + pedals, full Piano section (including SUSTPED/PSTICK routing via Shift + Layer A/B), full Organ section (B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe 1/B3 Bass/Pipe 2 models, nine live drawbars, percussion including POLY mode, vib/chorus scanner, per-section SUSTPED/PSTICK, ORGAN rotary routing, the PRESET / Drawbar Live per-layer toggle with SYNC as its Shift pairing (manual p. 19/21), and a section-inspect/zoom overlay for narrow viewports), the complete Synth section (section on/off, three layers with enable/focus/level/octave/zones/SUSTPED/PSTICK and their own independent effect chains via FX FOCUS SYNTH, the full Analog-mode waveform list plus the optional-scope Sub Osc/Shape/Shape Sine/Wave/FM-I categories, category-correct Osc Ctrl, the Amp/Filter/Osc Envelope buttons, the filter including the optional LP M/LP+HP types, LFO, Voice Mode/priority, Glide, Synth Unison, Vibrato Mode including the optional Delayed/Pedal sub-modes, the arpeggiator/gate, Synth Mode's Analog<->Samples cycle, Sound Init (Shift + Waveform Select — the panel's one red-framed button, manual p. 37), and the Osc Pitch view (PITCH/SMP latches the OLED dials onto -24..+24 st + ±50 c per layer, manual p. 28)), full Layer Effects section including FX Focus Synth, Rotary strip (drive/speed/stop/source), Master Level, pitch stick (±2 semitones per section while its PSTICK is on), Panic, Programs (32 bank slots + 8 Live slots, Store/Store As/undo, navigation, and the three PRESET LIBRARY buttons — manual p. 41-42: dial-browse/load of factory banks (14 Synth presets, 12 Organ registrations across all six models, 13 Piano presets over the eight bundled instruments) with a Cancel soft button, SINGLE LAYER via Shift for Piano/Synth (Organ presets are always whole-Section, p. 41 note), and the p. 43 Layer-Scene rule (a Section load turns that Section off in the non-active scene)), Splits/zones/Layer Scenes (with SET KEY = Shift + Split nudging the selected split point, manual p. 39, and press-and-hold opening the point editor), Morph assignment (Wheel/A.T./Control Pedal — A.T. moves from MIDI channel pressure), Master Clock and Transpose, Monitor/Copy/Paste (manual p. 43, pointer-first adaptation: the Mon/Copy click latches a read-only monitor/copy mode — continuous controls display their canonical value without writing, Layer/effect ON/Morph/PROGRAM buttons copy — and Shift + Mon/Copy latches Paste, with a repeat Mon/Copy press toggling Paste ⇄ Swap (manual p. 43) — Swap interchanges the copied layer's current state and chain with the pressed same-section layer's; same-section layer pastes, same-unit effect pastes, morph pastes onto the pressed source and program pastes into the pressed slot, with incompatible targets truthfully refused), and Shift as the modifier for Global mode, SUSTPED/PSTICK and the various Shift-paired menu actions. The ARP MENU button is functional too (manual p. 35-36: a latched Synth-OLED dial mode across all five pages — Direction/Zig Zag plus the Pattern Preset/Length/Edit/Accent/Pan pages), as are PATTERN (Shift + Arp Mode) and GROUP (Shift + Arp Menu — an adaptation: the section-level arp drives all enabled layers or just the focused one). Morph A.T. is functional too: its button arms assignments like the other sources and the source value moves from MIDI channel pressure (0xD0) — the one aftertouch input browsers can deliver. Only Synth Mode's Extern position stays truthfully decorative.

The Organ section (all layers) and each Synth layer route through their own instance of the same ordered effect chain as a Piano layer (Mod 1 → Mod 2 → Delay → Amp Sim/EQ → Compressor → Reverb); FX focus follows whichever section/layer was last pressed, moving the panel's effect knobs, Group/Global mirroring and morph capture onto that chain.

Programs are a showcase extension beyond the sealed benchmark scope: 32 bank slots (4 pages x 8) + 8 auto-storing Live slots snapshot all supported piano/organ/synth/effects/routing/split/scene/morph/clock/transpose state (Master Level excluded per spec), with Store/Store As naming flows, truthful dirty-E/edit-discard semantics, single-level undo, Shift+dial list view, and persistence through an injectable storage boundary (localStorage in the browser; no audio is stored — snapshots are parameter JSON only).

Splits and Layer Scenes are functional: 3 editable split points (11 documented positions, Off/±6/±12 crossfades that scale voice gains complementarily) partition the keybed into up to 4 zones; each piano/organ/synth layer holds a contiguous KB ZONE assignment (Shift+Octave); Scene I/II swaps layer enables only.

Morph assignment is functional for all three sources — Wheel, A.T. and Control Pedal: latching a source button captures start→end ranges on the morphable destinations (layer levels, drawbars — inapplicable while that organ layer is in Drawbar Live mode, manual p. 39 — rotary speed, effect rates/amounts/mixes); the mod wheel (on-screen or MIDI CC1), MIDI channel pressure (0xD0 — A.T. has no on-screen input of its own, since browsers deliver aftertouch only via MIDI), and an on-screen Control Pedal slider or MIDI CC11 interpolate them live as performance inputs (no dirty flag). LED ladders (layer faders, organ drawbars) show the assigned range as dim half-opacity LEDs. Master Clock (30-300 BPM; tap or dial-edit; syncs Delay time and Mod 1/Arp rate per chain) and Transpose (-6..+6 st on sounding pitch) are functional and program-stored.

Deterministic tests cross the real audio boundary via node-web-audio-api OfflineAudioContext rendering (no network, devices or audio output); browser boundaries (context, assets, MIDI, timers) remain injectable and fake-backed state tests complement, not replace, the rendered-audio proofs.
